landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?

landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?

landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?

site.seo.faq1_a: Upload a source video and clear reference images, then choose the editing mode or a ready-made template. Genjutsu AI can preserve motion and camera timing while changing selected visual elements. Available capabilities depend on the feature and its safety checks.
site.seo.faq2_q: Does Genjutsu AI support face swapping?
site.seo.faq2_a: Some Genjutsu AI templates support changing a character's appearance using authorized images, while other tools have different input restrictions. Only use images you have the right to edit, get consent where needed, and do not impersonate people or create misleading content. Upload clear images and check each tool's requirements before generating. See our Terms of Service (/terms-of-service) for prohibited content and enforcement.
site.seo.faq3_q: How is this different from text-to-video?
site.seo.faq3_a: You start with a real take. The model does not invent a new camera path from a prompt alone. It transfers or preserves the motion already in the file you upload.
site.seo.faq4_q: What can I change in a clip?
site.seo.faq4_a: Scenes, styles, products, and props. Aim for a full environment restage, a style filter, or a local object swap — while keeping the original subject intact.
site.seo.faq5_q: Do I need a Higgsfield subscription?
site.seo.faq5_a: No. This site sells prepaid credit packs and charges per generation. The official Higgsfield product is subscription-based if you prefer to work there instead.
site.seo.faq6_a: Each job is estimated from the provider cost for your input duration and resolution. Input length is rounded up to the next whole second. The exact credit reserve is calculated on the server before generation starts.
site.seo.faq7_q: How long does a generation take?
site.seo.faq7_a: Typical jobs finish in minutes, depending on clip length, resolution, and queue. You can leave the page and check status; the task is tracked on the server.
site.seo.faq8_a: 480p, 720p, and 1080p. Higher resolution costs more credits because the provider charges more per second of input video.
site.seo.faq9_q: Can I use the output commercially?
site.seo.faq9_a: You may use generated videos subject to our Terms of Service, applicable AI provider policies, and relevant law. Only upload content you are authorized to edit.

site.hotel.trend_p3: It is not a traditional camera filter. The versions people share are generated or edited with AI from reference images and a motion or scene template. This page packages that generation step into one preset.

Creators film themselves — or, most famously, their parents — dancing as if the song never left the club: shoulders pulsing, arms swinging, big emotional faces, and an unmistakable mid-80s attitude.
site.smalltown.seo.what_p2: It is a challenge, not a fixed choreography drop. Unlike K-pop tutorials with official counts, there is no single licensed move list. That open brief is why the same audio can host a dad in the kitchen, a dual-dancer depth swap, or an AI face-mapped recreation of the template staging.
site.smalltown.seo.origin_p1: "Smalltown Boy" is Bronski Beat's debut single, released on 25 May 1984 by London Recordings and later included on the album The Age of Consent. It was written by Steve Bronski, Jimmy Somerville, and Larry Steinbachek, produced by Mike Thorne, and sits at the intersection of synth-pop, hi-NRG, and disco. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 163 on its list of the greatest dance songs; in the United States it reached No. 48 on the pop chart and No. 1 on the dance chart.

site.flying_car.seo.real_p1: The Roadster clip is real. Tesla filmed it at a closed test site in front of a live crowd on October 15, 2026, and streamed it on X and YouTube. It shows short hops, one mid-air roll, and a car clearing a row of stationary vehicles.
site.flying_car.seo.real_p2: What it is not: a car cruising over a city. The real thing runs on cold-gas thrusters — compressed air, roughly 600 liters of it — plus fans that hold the car against a curved ramp. That buys a couple of seconds of airtime. Every clip you've seen of a flying car gliding between skyscrapers, weaving through traffic lanes in the sky, or landing on a helipad is AI-generated.
site.flying_car.seo.real_rule: So the rule is simple: ground-level hops on thrusters are real; altitude and cruising are fake.
site.flying_car.seo.spot_title: How to spot a fake flying car video in 5 seconds
site.flying_car.seo.spot1: Look at the wheels. Rims melt, spokes blur into a single smear, and wheels spin at the wrong speed or not at all. This is the single most reliable tell.
site.flying_car.seo.spot2: Read the text. License plates, badges and background shop signs turn to gibberish or wobble.
site.flying_car.seo.spot3: Check the reflection. The car's reflection won't match the sky, the ground, or the other cars around it.
site.flying_car.seo.spot4: Trace the source. If a clip only exists as an anonymous repost with no original link, treat it as generated.
site.flying_car.seo.spot5: Check the altitude. Thrusters hop. They don't cruise. Airborne at building height = AI.
site.flying_car.seo.spot_note: Genjutsu is an AI video tool — label AI-generated exports when you post. If a clip of yours spreads, keep that label with it.
